subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Which public contract should OpenClaw support for user-scoped skill preferences, if any: a markdown sidecar beside the skill, a structured config surface, or no core contract?
rationale: The choice changes skill precedence, prompt snapshots, watcher invalidation, config surface area, and security/root-containment behavior, so implementation should wait for maintainer product/API direction.

options.title: Approve markdown sidecar
options.body: Standardize a markdown preference sidecar and require loader, prompt-version, watcher, docs, and regression-test coverage.

options.title: Use structured config
options.body: Model preferences as canonical configuration and require schema, docs, and doctor/migration decisions before implementation.

options.title: Keep agent-managed convention only
options.body: Do not add a core contract and document that users should keep conventions inside custom skills or skill-owned docs.

recommendation.title: Approve markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Standardize a markdown preference sidecar and require loader, prompt-version, watcher, docs, and regression-test coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The current loader and prompt-contract lines are blamed to Peter Steinberger and he has the strongest recent history on the affected skill-loading/docs surface.
